summary: The candidate captures all central paper-specific results and most of the external infrastructure, with generally accurate pages, entry classes, hypotheses, and formulas. It is nevertheless not flawless: it systematically mistranslates stable cohomotopy as stable cohomology, omits two foundational definitions and a standalone precise Taubes theorem, duplicates Lemma 2.6, drops the non-torsion hypothesis from that lemma, and formats two mod-4 hypotheses ambiguously.
strengths: Correctly captures the main Theorem 1.4, Theorem 1.9, Theorems 2.3 and 2.4, Lemma 3.1, and the sphere obstruction corresponding to Theorem 2.8.
Accurately extracts the definitions of geometrically simply connected manifolds and classes represented by a 2-handle neighborhood, with appropriate fact/definition classification.
Includes the key Bauer connected-sum theorem and Frøyshov vanishing theorem as external results with accurate source attribution and page locators.
Represents the symplectic Betti-number parity input and the Taubes input in partial form, and correctly marks them as external.
Adds relevant paper results beyond the Gold set, including Corollaries 1.6 and 1.7 and the PL-embedded-sphere characterization.
LaTeX is generally balanced, readable, and mathematically interpretable.
issues: The phrase "稳定上同调 Seiberg–Witten 不变量" is used repeatedly for stable cohomotopy/Bauer–Furuta invariants; "稳定上同伦" or an equally precise stable-cohomotopy term is required. This is a systematic mathematical terminology error affecting several core entries.
The Bauer–Furuta invariant itself is not extracted as a definition, although it is foundational in the Gold reference.
The definition of a symplectic form and its induced canonical spin^c structure is missing.

The Taubes result is not captured as the standalone statement SW_X(s_X)=±1, hence nonzero mod 2. The candidate only records the narrower consequence used when both orientations are assumed symplectic.
Both yasui:lemma:2-6 and yasui:lemma:2-handle-sphere encode essentially the same result, creating an unnecessary duplicate.
The two versions of Lemma 2.6 omit the Gold reference's non-torsion hypothesis on alpha, thereby stating a potentially broader claim than the verified entry.

The candidate writes the doubled class as alpha-bar alpha, whereas the Gold notation is alpha times bar alpha. This may reflect a notation convention, but it should be checked because subtraction can suggest a different homology class.
The congruence hypotheses in Theorems 1.9 and 2.4 are malformed or ambiguous: mod 4 is visibly attached only to the b_2^- condition, while both b_2^+ and b_2^- conditions should be modulo 4.
Entries yasui:theorem:1-6 and yasui:theorem:1-7 are classified with type and claimKind "theorem" even though their own names and the source identify them as corollaries.

The external adjunction-inequality and blow-up-formula entries are overly vague compared with the otherwise precise extraction standard and do not delimit the hypotheses and conclusions needed to function as reliable mathematical entries.
The artifact contains no inference hints, so the proof dependency structure among the definitions, external results, intermediate lemmas, and main theorems is not represented.
